producer_report.summary: Root cause: nothing compared a finished prompt file, or the entries a change appends to docs/decisions.md, with the structure they must keep before verification. So job 20261015-095214-y8kr (two bullets joined in reader.md) and job 20261025-034452-wqp8 (D122 inserted inside D121) were found only at the final verdict. Fix, in the mirror registry (crates/athena-core/src/mirrors.rs), which mirror_drift_in and the candidate gate already run: two new Rule variants and two REGISTRY entries, with no new call site. (1) PromptStructure, glob crates/*/prompts/*.md, each file its own mirror via new Mirror::files and Mirror::covers. It judges only added lines. A base list item that now sits mid-line after a sentence end is a finding. An added list item with a second item glued after it is a finding, but only when an item head (`name:` or the next number) follows the second marker, so `one- or two-line` and `*Never do X.* Then` are not flagged. (2) DecisionEntries judges only entries after the end of the base, when the base is an exact prefix: shaped heading, next id, Provenance inside the entry's own span. The decision log now has one parser (parse_decision_entries, decision_log_problems), also called by the athena-cli log guard check_log. append_only_problem names the entry (`in D121`, or `before D122` for an insertion at a heading). Tests: unit tests in mirrors.rs on the exact shapes of both jobs plus no-false-positive cases; mirrors_ tests in run/tests.rs that drive the real producer loop and show the break is sent back once and a fix reaches the verifier; fixture arms in the athena-cli mirrors test; one log-guard/rule parity test. D162 (amends D158 in prose only) and its decision-links.toml link record the change; CHANGELOG Unreleased entry added. Three files outside the listed deliverables changed because the change needs them: crates/athena-cli/tests/mirrors.rs (exhaustive match on Rule would not compile), crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs (producer-step tests), crates/athena-cli/src/decisions.rs (single log definition). Limits: structure only, not intent; other file classes and changelog truth not covered.

open_issues: The rules judge structure, not intent: a wrong word on the right line, or a join with a reworded head and no marker, still reaches the verifier. Findings 2 and 3 of job 20261015-095214-y8kr (an untrue changelog claim, unexplained trimming) are out of scope.
Other file classes with the same free-text risk (docs/design/*.md and others) are not covered; adding one is a single REGISTRY entry plus a rule.
The full `cargo test --locked` run exited 0, but its output was too large to inspect for per-target counts; the targeted runs above I did read.
The replay of accepted readings is Athena's check; I did not run it. The change touches no reading or planning code.
mistakes: I first wrote heading_id with the wrong slice length (3..3+digits dropped the last digit); the new tests caught it.
Two of my own tests had wrong expectations (`D06` instead of `D6` in the message text; `from` = 0 where the base length was needed); I fixed the tests and left the code unchanged.
A byte-string literal with the middle-dot character did not compile; I switched to str::as_bytes.
learnings: Mirror.mirror was always a plain file path; check_all, watches, check_entry's drift stamp and the athena-cli fixture all assumed that. A glob needed Mirror::files and Mirror::covers and a concrete Drift.mirror.

athena-cli's check_log already held a second definition of a well-formed decision log; it now calls athena_core::mirrors::decision_log_problems, with unshaped headings and the next-id rule applied only from the pinned length.

backtest's phrase scan is a case-insensitive substring match on `amends`, `supersedes` and `superseded by` per line, so a new decision entry may contain only one such phrase, on one line, and decision-links.toml needs its line number.
Rust 1.97 and edition 2024 allow let-chains in this repository.
The Bash tool allows only cargo, git, ls, chmod, mv and rm, so no grep or tail; and a path outside the working directory (such as the persisted tool-output file) cannot be read.
desires: A way to read the persisted output of a long cargo test run (or a quieter test output mode) to confirm per-target counts.
A machine-readable intended edit in the job (for example the lines the plan expects to change) would let a later check compare the finished diff with intent, not only with structure.
